title: Africa outline map
subject: Geography
source: Written for geography/y7 lesson 20 (Africa outline map (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 20: What and where is Africa?. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Where is Africa?
points: South of Europe across the Mediterranean
Atlantic to the west, Indian Ocean to the east
Joined to Asia at the Suez area

panels.title: A huge continent
points: Second largest by population: over 1.4 billion

parts.text: Crossed by the Equator, so in both hemispheres
South of Europe across the Mediterranean
South-west of Asia, across the Red Sea
Atlantic to the west, Indian Ocean to the east

keywords.def: one of seven very large land masses
the line of latitude at 0 degrees
the lines of latitude about 23.5 degrees north and south
an over-simple idea about a group or place
one narrow picture told about a place or people

questions.q: Which sea separates Africa from Europe?
Which ocean lies east of Africa?
Which three lines of latitude cross Africa?
questions.a: The Equator, the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn

questions.q: Core: On the outline map, label Africa's surrounding seas and oceans, the Equator and tropics, the Suez Canal, and write a location paragraph.
questions.a: Accurate labels and a paragraph using hemispheres, neighbours and oceans

questions.q: Extend: List five facts that challenge a 'single story' of Africa.
questions.a: For example: 54 countries; Lagos is a megacity; Timbuktu had famous libraries; the Sahara and rainforests; fast-growing tech sector

questions.q: Stretch: Where do single stories come from, and how can geographers avoid them?
questions.a: News and films showing one side; use many sources and data from many places

questions.q: How many countries are there in Africa?
questions.a: B) 54. Africa has 54 countries; it is a continent, not a country.

questions.q: Big question: where did your picture of Africa come from?
questions.a: Reflection naming a source and how today's facts change it
